svg.text: The attr column of info mem is the flag bits of the entry, one letter each, in the order r w x u g a d
V has no letter: info mem
code: read, execute, user; accessed, never written
guard page: no u, so a user program may not touch it
stack: read, write, user; accessed and dirty (written)
heap page just added: read, write, user; never touched
a letter = that bit is 1; a dash = 0
Why a missing u bit is a fence
on the guard page: no u bit →
Hardware checks V and U together
On every access from a user program the MMU reads
the row and checks: is it valid, and may the user touch it?
A row without u fails the second check, so to the
program it is just as untouchable as a page with no row.
The trap is the same trap (scause 13 load, 15 store).
